request.system:
You write short rationales for UK property ownership structure options shown to an investment committee.
Rules: each rationale is at most 2 sentences, plain English, and contains NO numbers, digits, percentages or money amounts.
Never state tax amounts or rates. Describe why the structure might suit this packet and investors, and its main trade-off.
Return JSON: {"A": string, "B": string, "C": string, "D": string}.
request.user:
Packet: 6 properties; residential residential in england.
Contains residential dwellings: yes.
Investors: UK family office.
Option A: Buy each property directly. Chain: UK family office -> properties.
Option B: One UK SPV owns the portfolio. Chain: UK family office -> PropCo Ltd -> properties.
Option C: Fund (unit trust) owns the SPV. Chain: UK family office -> RIF -> PropCo Ltd -> properties.
Option D: Family trust owns the SPV. Chain: UK family office (settlor) -> Discretionary trust -> PropCo Ltd -> properties.

response.A: Direct ownership is the simplest route for a family office, with no company or trust to run and the income and gains flowing straight through. The trade-off is that each residential property has to be bought and sold separately, and the properties stay inside the family's own estate for inheritance planning.
response.B: One SPV lets the family office hold all the residential properties as a single package, keeps the income inside a company and could make a later sale through a share transfer simpler. The trade-off is that a company owning dwellings can face extra residential charges and higher purchase costs, and there is a second layer of tax when profits are taken out.
response.C: A unit trust fund over the SPV gives a structured, tax-efficient wrapper and makes it easier to bring in outside co-investors alongside the family. The trade-off is significant set-up cost, regulation and eligibility conditions that may be hard for a single family office to meet.
response.D: A discretionary trust over the SPV suits a family office focused on passing wealth down the generations and keeping flexible control over who benefits. The trade-off is inheritance tax charges when assets go in and at regular anniversaries, plus extra trust administration and reporting.
